value.body: A plantation officer raises tree seedlings and manages plantations. Many work for paper and wood-based companies that grow trees with farmers, or for carbon, agroforestry and restoration projects. Days are spent in nurseries, on plantation sites and visiting farmers.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc Forestry (some employers also take agriculture graduates)

items.label: Where you work
items.value: Nurseries, plantation sites and villages, mostly in rural areas

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join a paper or wood-based company, an agroforestry project or an NGO as a field or plantation trainee. Nursery and field training from the degree is directly useful.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Working with farmers and field staff

value.title: At a glance
items: The work is outdoors and travel-heavy.
It can lead to plantation manager or raw-material manager roles.
Experience overlaps with agroforestry, carbon-project and NGO work.
